items.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: And so Jimmy says, “You want to do this thing?”

ctx.x: Oh yeah, he’s great. I love Bill Berry. Bill Berry, myself and a very fine musician from the Santa Cruz area named Paul Contos, a reed player, very good. The three of us started.

And when they tapped me I had worked the festival a few times with Cal Tjader and some other people. And so Jimmy says, “You want to do this thing?” And I said, “I’m not a teacher, I wouldn’t know where to begin.” I mean it’s true, I mean you need an educator. He said, “Nope, Mundell said we want players just to go in and impart your experience.” I said, “Okay I’ll try it.” Twenty years later, you know? It’s fun. I enjoy that. I really do.

Well I think it’s an important thing that teachers of jazz — and I suppose you could say this about anything, but especially of jazz, ought to be players first. And I’m not sure that’s the norm anymore in the universities.
